newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Lee says no to "one country, two systems".
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Lee says no to "one country, two systems".

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui on Monday ruled out re-unification with arch-rival China under Beijing's "one country, two systems" proposal.
He also said Taiwan needed submarines to defend its coast against possible Chinese aggression.
"We cannot accept ... the 'one country, two systems' proposal. It is impossible," Lee told German television in an interview.

China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, has proposed that the two rivals unite according to the "one country, two systems" proposal under which Hong Kong will return to Chinese rule from July 1.
China has promised that the now-British colony's capitalist system will be allowed to remain intact for 50 years after the handover.

"There is a basic problem we should think about. China is a divided state. Here is the Republic of China government on Taiwan, and on the mainland is the People's Republic of China government," Lee said in a statement released by the Presidential Office.

"When (Chinese paramount leader) Deng Xiaoping proposed 'one country, two systems', what is this 'one country' which is referred to? Does it mean the People's Republic of China or the Republic of China? It is not clear.
"Under these circumstances, making such a proposal is unreasonable," he said.

Lee defended his government's purchases of foreign weapons by citing the threat of military action by China, which has repeatedly warned that should the island officially seek independence from the mainland it will reclaim Taiwan by force.
"We absolutely will not resort to military force to provoke (China) and start a war. This is what the Chinese communists have always done," Lee said without elaborating.
But he stressed Taiwan needed submarines "to maintain stability in the Taiwan Strait and protect ourselves".
Beijing staged wargames and conducted missile tests in the Taiwan Strait between August 1995 and March 1996, angered by a trip to the United States by Lee in June 1995.

"The biggest problem we are facing is a lack of submarines. If a Taiwan Strait war is waged, the Republic of China faces the threat of being blockaded. Therefore, sumbarines are a must to safeguard the Republic of China," he said.
He asked Germany to resist Chinese pressure and sell submarines to Taiwan. Taiwan has for years pressed Germany to sell it submarines but Bonn has refused out of fear of upsetting China.

Lee also warned other countries not to be seduced by the vast potential of mainland China's markets, saying investors must consider the risks before investing there because "Chinese laws are changing almost every day".
"It is true that many Taiwanese firms have invested on the mainland, but it is also true that they have faced many problems in their operations there," he said.
Some 30,000 Taiwan businessmen have poured more than US$25 billion into mainland investments.
